title: Root-cause fingerprint alert deduplication with dynamic thresholds
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We continue to see excessive pager noise from transient capacity regressions and autoscaler oscillations. Current burn-rate and threshold rules generate pages for many alerts that share a common root cause, causing duplicated work and extended incident cycles. Goal: reduce actionable pager volume by ~40% without increasing miss rate on high-impact SLO breaches. Approach: implement a deduplication layer that groups alerts by a root-cause fingerprint and applies dynamic, impact-weighted thresholds and cooldowns per fingerprint. The system should be conservative by default and allow gradual relaxation for low-impact, repeated flapping signals.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce page count for SLO burn alerts by >=35% in canary orgs within 4 weeks
No increase in P1 customer-impacting SLO breaches attributable to dedup logic
Dashboard showing per-fingerprint page reduction and false-suppression incidents
Ability to opt a customer/project out via route config in Console
work_items: Design fingerprint schema (error class + stack-signature + topology tags + recent-event-hash)
Prototype fingerprinting service (Go) with Redis-backed TTL store
Prometheus/Alertmanager rule shim to emit fingerprint labels
Policy engine: per-fingerprint cooldown, dynamic threshold multiplier, decay window
PagerDuty stage mapping + fallback rules integration
Create Console UI config to view/override fingerprint policies
E2E tests and chaos scenarios (autoscaler oscillation, KV cache eviction bursts)
Run 2-week canary on non-production orgs then expand
notes_and_decisions: 2026-02-27 - Decision: Use fingerprints rather than full causal analysis to keep latency low and avoid central graph computations (Priya Khatri, Diego Ramos)
2026-03-01 - Trade-off: TTL-based dedup reduces pages but risks delaying unique regressions; we will gate by customer_impact weighting and a fast-path for high-severity SLO breaches (Ava Chen)
2026-03-04 - Implementation detail: fingerprint will include normalized error message, model variant, region, and first 8 bytes of stack hash to reduce cardinality (engineering design doc linked)
2026-03-06 - Observability: add 'fingerprint_id' to existing SLO burn metrics and traces to enable post-hoc false-suppression audits
safety_considerations: Ensure dedup logic cannot suppress alerts for customers with 'strict-paging' contract; add allowlist by org/route. Maintain audit log of suppressed pages for 90 days.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated; 2) Canary on infra-dev and 2 non-prod orgs for 2 weeks; 3) Enable for low-traffic customers (10%) and monitor key metrics for 2 weeks; 4) Gradually expand by 25% every week if no regressions; 5) Full rollout with postmortem after 8 weeks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive suppression hides real regressions - Mitigation: conservative defaults, fast-path for high severity, kill-switch in Console
Risk: Fingerprint cardinality explosion - Mitigation: normalize and bucket stack signatures, use sampling for rare events
Risk: Increased alerting latency due to extra lookup - Mitigation: Redis TTL store colocated with alerting shims; benchmark acceptable (<50ms)
Risk: Confusing ownership when multiple teams affected - Mitigation: include contributing services in fingerprint and enrich PagerDuty payloads with context
qa_and_testing: Unit tests for fingerprint normalization, integration tests with Alertmanager shim, load test under synthetic autoscaler oscillation scenario, and manual runbook drill with on-call rotation. Include a synthetic canary that injects duplicate alerts to validate dedup behavior.
next_steps: Assign engineering pair to prototype (Diego + Lila Park), schedule design review with SRE and Console PM, open initial PR for fingerprint schema and Alertmanager shim, and create canary org config in Console.
